2. TECHNICAL RECONCILIATION & SYSTEM CONTRADICTIONS
---------------------------------------------------
An engineering audit of the codebase reveals several systemic vulnerabilities:

* THE "FALSE MONITORING" GAP:
  - The Status Dot indicators on Command Control previously reported a false green status because they only probed process existence on the host machine. If a service was running but hit an API auth block (like the HTTP 401 on your DeepSeek bot), the system still reported "OK".
  - SOLUTION APPLIED: I have integrated true AJAX-level polling in "index.html". It now performs active HTTP status fetches, checks queue logs on disk, and flags any 401 unauthorized errors immediately on the server grid.

* ARCHITECTURAL REDUNDANCIES:
  - The name "agent-daemon.js" is a gross contradiction. It contains Next.js frontend code rather than actual daemon process loops.
  - The Express backend "server.js" has hardcoded secrets (Redis ports, model keys). These must be immediately segregated into a local ".env" file.

3. INVENTORY & SUGGESTED EXTENSIONS
-----------------------------------
- Active Resources: Docker Compose, Nginx (port 80), Redis (6379), Prometheus (9090), OpenClaw Gateway (18789), and Express.js (3000).
- Proposed Extension — Automated Rebuild Watcher: Integration of a filesystem watcher (using nodemon or chokidar) that automatically executes "docker compose up -d --build" whenever "server.js" or local config files are edited. This eliminates the risk of stale containers running old code silently.
- Proposed Extension — Local Vector Storage: An MCP bridge to a lightweight Milvus or SQLite-vector database to store system logs and session trajectories for auditability.

4. CONCLUSION SUMMARY
---------------------
Engineering decisions must always be based on quality. We have successfully aligned Command Control to report absolute, real-time truth. Our next steps are to move from periodic crons to a true continuous execution daemon, ensuring our agent network is fully resilient to restarts and network failures.
